compiled_state.description:
## The hazard

Every concurrent Claude/agent session on this host pushes, amends and submits Gerrit changes under
the SAME `RebarBotNava` identity. Gerrit therefore reports `owner:self` for changes belonging to
other sessions, and there is no field anywhere in the change that says which session is driving it.
Ownership is invisible at exactly the moment it matters: when deciding whether to amend or submit.

## Two instances, both on 2026-09-04/05

**(1) A submit raced a live rebase by 39 seconds.** An orchestrator saw change 2645 at
`LLM-Review +1` / `Verified +1` and attempted to submit it. Gerrit refused with `HTTP 409` (rebase
conflict on `docs/env-vars.md`), so the orchestrator dispatched an agent to rebase and re-push.
That agent's first act was to check for a concurrent owner, and found:

- patch set 4 had been uploaded **39 seconds earlier** (02:35:39 UTC; the check ran at 02:36:18);
- `current_revision` was already `10af5f28bcaf`, not the `56787a044821` the submit had failed on;
- a worktree at `/Users/joeoakhart/reb-640-terraform-grounding` held `10af5f28bcaf` with a reflog
  showing `rebase (start)` -> `rebase (continue)` -> `rebase (finish)` — another session had
  resolved the identical conflict minutes before.

Had the agent proceeded it would have pushed a competing patch set 5 over 39-second-old work. It
was stopped only because the dispatch brief happened to include an ownership check. Nothing in the
system would have prevented it.

**(2) A subagent misattributed a merge to a third party.** Earlier the same night a subagent
reported that change 2642 "merged without it submitting", treating it as an anomaly worth
investigating. The submitter was its own orchestrator. The subagent could not tell, because both
act as `RebarBotNava`.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than working around

The two failure directions are asymmetric and both bad. Case (1) is a WRITE race that silently
discards another session's work; case (2) is wasted investigation into a phantom. Neither is
detectable after the fact from the change itself.

It also interacts badly with the vote model: an upload marks prior votes **Outdated**, so a
competing patch set does not merely duplicate effort — it RESETS two gates that had already passed,
returning the change to the back of a saturated CI queue. In case (1) that is exactly what
happened: 2645's `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` from PS3 are both listed as Outdated on PS4, so
a change that was submittable now has zero live votes.

## Directions (none endorsed; the ticket is the problem statement)

- Per-session Gerrit identities, so `owner` is meaningful. Highest fidelity, largest credential and
  access-control cost; note `RebarBotNava`'s Contributor rights would need replicating per identity.
- A machine-local claim registry mapping change number -> worktree/session, written on push and
  read before amend/submit. Cheap, but advisory only, and another session can ignore it.
- Make the check mandatory rather than remembered: document (and script) the pre-submit
  verification the agent above performed by luck of its brief — confirm `current_revision` matches
  what you inspected, confirm votes are live rather than Outdated, and check `git worktree list`
  for a local holder before amending someone else's change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The ownership question is answerable BEFORE an amend or submit, by a documented and scripted
      check rather than by an agent happening to think of it.
- [ ] A submit is refused, or at minimum loudly warned, when the `current_revision` differs from
      the revision whose votes were inspected. Proven by attempting a submit against a
      deliberately stale revision and observing the refusal.
- [ ] The interaction with vote invalidation is stated wherever the push flow is documented: an
      unnecessary patch set RESETS `LLM-Review` and `Verified` to Outdated and re-queues the
      change, so re-pushing a green change is destructive, not neutral.
- [ ] Whichever direction is chosen is recorded with its reasoning, including an explicit decision
      on per-session identities (adopt or reject with a reason) rather than defaulting to the
      cheapest option by omission.
compiled_state.title: Concurrent sessions share one RebarBotNava Gerrit identity, so change ownership is invisible: a submit raced another session's rebase by 39 seconds and would have reset two passing gates
